A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same quantized-SGD linear-regression research. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and the reorganized proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 1 report original Gaussian linear-regression simulations varying quantization strength and dimension.

after.justification: The original simulations remain, supplemented by Communities and Crime regression, covariance-spectrum measurements, and additional synthetic experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The main quantized-SGD procedure is retained. Appendix F adds a variant that quantizes the carried master weights, replacing the leading w(t-1) with Qp(w(t-1)) in Eq. (F.1). This is a limited but actual procedural extension.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from Gaussian regression with polynomial-decay covariance to real-world violent-crime-rate regression on Communities and Crime and synthetic regression with exponential-decay covariance. These introduce substantially different populations and feature distributions.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain full precision, additive quantization, and multiplicative quantization. The added experiments reuse these schemes; no additional competing optimizer or quantization method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The original Figure 1 settings remain unchanged. Appendix G adds experiments with B=10 and d=200, fixed quantization error 0.01 for Communities and Crime, and empirical covariance-spectrum measurements. Figure 1's revised population-risk caption clarifies the reported quantity without establishing a changed metric.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained quantization-strength and dimension sweeps, v2 adds a direct examination of covariance-spectrum distortion and sensitivity tests for larger batches and exponential spectral decay. Figures 2(b) and 3 substantially broaden the empirical checks of the proposed mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The new figures do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1's plots are unchanged. New Figures 2–3 report that multiplicative quantization stays close to full-precision performance on Communities and Crime, preserves covariance structure better, and retains favorable behavior under larger batches and exponential spectra. These are additional findings under new settings, not improvements to existing same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects the sign of a quantization contribution and cancels label terms, supporting a revised three-component bound in Theorem 4.1. Theorems and corollaries receive new bounds and conditions; Assumption 4.1 introduces an isotropic parameter prior; Appendix F adds master-weight proofs. Appendix E also reformulates moment assumptions, although its new Eq. (E.16) appears to omit the label-noise contribution proportional to H.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions replace the claim that data and label quantization introduce approximation and separate quantized errors with approximation error attributed to data quantization. They also replace elimination of spectral distortion with preservation of spectral structure and reduced distortion. These materially revise the central characterization of quantization effects.

C2.justification: V2 develops the additive noise-floor and signal-dependent-noise explanations, adds consequences of quantizing master weights, and revises the practical FP-versus-integer bit-width comparison from a half-logarithmic dimension term to one scaled by the spectral exponent a. These change substantive interpretations and applicability guidance.

D1.justification: Appendix G documents the exponential spectrum, Communities and Crime's sources and approximate dimensions, and experiment-specific quantization and batch settings. Reproducibility remains limited: preprocessing, data splits, numerical learning rates, and code-access information are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds Li et al. (2025), Modoranu et al. (2024), and Ozkara et al. (2025), and removes Zou et al. (2021). These modestly update scaling-law and stochastic-quantization context while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the contributions, theoretical explanations, comparisons, and conclusion are rewritten. Additive quantization now precedes multiplicative quantization in Section 4.1, a notation paragraph is added, and the appendix narrative is reorganized around the revised decomposition.

P2.justification: V2 adds two figures containing six experimental panels and substantially redraws the proof-dependency diagram with larger, clearer nodes. Figure 1 retains its plots but receives a revised caption, while the appendix contents and equation layouts are reorganized.

improvement.justification: Correcting Appendix A's sign error and cancelling label terms repairs a central derivation underlying v1's risk characterization. The master-weight extension and new empirical checks add substantial theoretical scope and support. These gains outweigh a localized apparent omission in v2's Eq. (E.16), although that inequality needs correction and experimental reproducibility remains limited.
